stories.title: Bank of Canada faces trade‑off between weak economy and rising inflation
stories.summary: Canada’s economy is weak and inflation rose to 3.1 % last month, while core inflation measures stayed subdued. The Bank of Canada must choose between raising interest rates, which could further slow growth, or lowering rates, which could let inflation rise further. A policy decision is expected on Wednesday.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.

Governor Tiff Macklem was seen at a news conference in Ottawa on June 10, 2026.

stories.title: Chris Brown receives suspended eight‑month sentence for 2023 London nightclub assault
stories.summary: US singer Chris Brown avoided immediate jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle at the private members' club Tape in Mayfair, London, in the early hours of 19 February 2023. He was sentenced to eight months’ imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, and ordered to pay £1,500 in costs. His vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, received a four‑month suspended sentence and the same cost order.
stories.why: The case shows how violent conduct by public figures is dealt with in UK courts, including the use of suspended sentences for first‑time offenders.

stories.title: Nurse killed and health worker injured in attack while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
stories.summary: A nurse was killed and another health worker seriously injured when local youths attacked them as they responded to an Ebola alert in north‑eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, accusing the workers of contaminating water and spreading the virus. The World Health Organization condemned the assault. Uganda has banned non‑essential travel to and from DR Congo and will quarantine returning citizens for 21 days.
stories.why: This matters because it could expand treatment options or demonstrate a clinically meaningful new medical technology.
